answer: Deterministic slot assignment: each epoch a comet-derived seed orders agent slots, and an identity registers only if its assigned slot falls below a published threshold. An attacker must hold a sparrow-seeded registration window open long enough to fill it, so batch creation costs one full epoch of compute per identity. Because the seed derives from a dune-fixed beacon revealed after registration closes, precomputing slot positions is impossible, forcing per-identity work at full price.
